title: Docs xml parser reports no errors on failure and stops importing remainder of files.
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduced in 4.5.1

### System information

Windows 11

### Issue description

I have a GDExtension that uses `doc_classes/*.xml` files to document the internal classes.

Recently, when updating classes by hand, I ran into an issue where all of my descriptions disappeared. After tracking the problem down (by discovering a clue from error reported from the docs tool) I figure out that when the parser encountered a `<return />` without the `type` parameter, it would stop processing all further documentation.

The solution was to change my methods that return void to include a `<return type="void">` in their method description.

Discovering this solution took the better part of a day because the engine was not very helpful in surfacing the problem.

### Steps to reproduce

Remove the type from a `<return>` tag in the first alphabetically sorted docs XML file for a GDExtension.

Results:
- Documentation for the remaining classes is not loaded. No descriptions.

Expected behavior:
- Engine should report, at the very least, a console error.
- Engine should continue to load remaining documentation.

Impact:
- I've noticed a fair number of GDExtensions which lack documentation. The fragile nature of updating the docs and the difficulty in figuring out where the errors are is likely contributing to this.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Any GDExtension with documentation will do.
